high.title: Ibovespa falls with uncertainty over US-Iran negotiations; 5 things to know before investing today (21)
high.summary: The Ibovespa follows negative external sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainties, declining 0.64% to 176,228.08 points by 10:10 AM Brasília time. The USD/BRL pair rose 0.25% to R$ 5.0159, tracking broader dollar strength as the DXY gained 0.26% to 99.354 points. Political noise continues affecting markets, with coordination changes in Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign team following controversy over a R$ 134 million request for a film project. The combination of geopolitical tensions from the US-Iran situation and domestic political uncertainty is weighing on Brazilian assets. FX traders should monitor the real's performance against EM peers, while equity investors need to watch for further political developments that could impact market sentiment. The correlation between external risk-off moves and BRL weakness remains intact.

high.title: Petrobras (PETR4) adheres to fuel subsidies, eyeing pricing policy
high.summary: Petrobras' board approved the company's participation in the economic subsidy program for fuel producers and importers under Provisional Measure 1.358, which provides tax rebates on gasoline and diesel production/imports. This mechanism enables Petrobras to adjust fuel prices with reduced impact at gas stations amid rising oil prices from geopolitical tensions. The decision demonstrates the state-controlled company's alignment with government policy to manage inflation pressures from higher commodity prices. For investors, this reduces Petrobras' pricing flexibility but potentially stabilizes cash flows by minimizing political interference risks. Bond traders should note this could help contain inflationary pressures that might otherwise force more aggressive BCB tightening.

medium.title: Market optimistic about US and Iran; Ibovespa in dollars falls today (22)
medium.summary: Markets show optimism as investors await updates on US-Iran peace negotiations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's comments and Iranian press reports indicated progress in talks, boosting equities after a week of pressure from inflation concerns and potential rate hikes. However, Rubio emphasized any deal would be "unfeasible" if Iran maintains control over Strait of Ormuz navigation. Domestic political noise continues with Flávio Bolsonaro denying requests for Trump meetings.

medium.title: Iran says 35 vessels crossed Strait of Ormuz in last 24 hours
medium.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy reported 35 commercial vessels crossed the Strait of Ormuz in 24 hours under Iranian coordination and protection, including oil tankers and container ships. The statement reinforces Tehran's attempt to consolidate operational influence over navigation through the strait, which handles about one-fifth of global oil transport. This development impacts oil prices and commodity markets that affect Brazilian trade dynamics.

medium.title: Asian stocks close higher, with attention on US-Iran peace efforts
medium.summary: Asian markets closed higher on Friday as investors monitored diplomatic efforts for a US-Iran peace agreement. Japan's Nikkei led gains with a 2.68% rise to 63,339.07 points, driven by technology and electronics stocks. Reports circulated about preliminary peace agreement progress, though Reuters noted Iran's intention to maintain enriched uranium domestically. The positive external sentiment provides supportive backdrop for emerging market assets including Brazilian equities.

medium.title: Live: Ibovespa closes week watching American consumer
medium.summary: The Ibovespa closes the week tracking UK retail sales and US Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index. The summary mentions continued focus on geopolitical developments including Iran's control over Strait of Ormuz shipping and Bitcoin's 5% weekly decline. External economic data remains crucial for Brazilian market direction given correlation with global risk sentiment.
